reasoning: 7-year-old with acute abdominal pain, vomiting, refusal to walk or engage — behavior consistent with peritoneal irritation, raising concern for appendicitis/perforation.

Pediatric normal SBP for this age is roughly 90-110 mmHg; 84/60 is below expected range, suggesting possible early compensated shock despite normal HR/RR/SpO2 — children can mask hypotension until late.
Low-grade fever plus vomiting plus refusal to bear weight/engage suggests a surgical abdomen or evolving sepsis picture, which can decompensate quickly in children.

Given the combination of borderline hypotension for age and signs of a serious intra-abdominal process, this warrants upgrading from a routine ESI 3 abdominal pain case to ESI 2 to ensure rapid physician evaluation and resuscitation readiness.
Per ESI guidance, when torn between levels, err toward the more acute one, especially with atypical or subtle high-risk vital sign patterns in pediatric patients.

Vomiting with fever in a child <10 years
